Plans and conditions in the future
Your semester abroad is coming to an end soon. Marc, your fellow student, wants to know what you're planning after you return to Germany and when you'll see each other again.
Talk about your plans with cuando / en cuanto + subjunctive and explain with para que why you should stay in touch.

MeaningMoodExample
habit / alwaysindicativeCuando llego a casa, me ducho.
pastindicativeCuando llegué, no había nadie.
futuresubjunctiveCuando llegues, llámame.
Never the future tense after cuando: cuando llegarás → cuando llegues. (English works the same way: "when you arrive", not "when you will arrive".)
When I know the date, I'll tell you.
When you're in Berlin, call me.
When you arrive at the airport, send me a message.

para que is always followed by the subjunctive. English: "so that".

Last week before your flight home. Marc asks about your plans.
And what will you do when you get back to Germany?
After cuando referring to the future → subjunctive: vuelva.
And when are you coming back to Barcelona?
OK. Before you leave, we'll have a farewell party.

Hi, Jonas! I already know Friday is your last day. I can't believe it. Before you leave, I want to give you a little present, so don't plan anything for Thursday evening. When you're in Germany, send me photos of Mannheim so I can see where you live. And as soon as you have holidays, come back, OK? There's always a sofa for you here. We'll miss you a lot! Love, Laia
Reply to Laia: thank her, say what you'll do when you're back, and when you'll come again. (5–6 sentences)
